target.title: Collapse publication throughput details by default
target.body:
## What changed

- wrap the publication-only throughput metrics in a native details disclosure
- keep the six rate values collapsed by default so the review and publication cards stay visually aligned
- explain that the 15-minute hourly-equivalent rates react faster but are more burst-sensitive than the up-to-60-minute net rate
- add focused dashboard coverage for the disclosure markup, default state, and window guidance

## Why

The publication card rendered six extra throughput rows that have no counterpart in the review card. Those rows made the two dashboard cards look vertically misaligned. The metrics remain available on demand, while the always-visible guidance prevents operators from treating the 15-minute and up-to-60-minute rates as equivalent signals.

## Validation

- `node --test test/dashboard-worker.test.ts`
- `pnpm run check`
- `/data/code/openclaw/openclaw/.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` (clean after one accepted copy correction)

target.title: fix(validation): allow inert install configs
target.body:
## Summary

- allow empty or comment-only `.npmrc` and `bunfig.toml` files during target dependency setup
- keep every active or unknown package-manager directive fail-closed
- cover registry, auth, proxy, certificate, fetch, unknown-setting, and bare-CR bypass cases

## Root cause

After the sparse-checkout repair in https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/630, automerge workers reached target toolchain setup but failed because the validation policy rejected the mere presence of `.npmrc`. OpenClaw retains a comment-only `.npmrc` so Docker COPY paths stay stable, as seen in https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29543195892.

This change permits only text that cannot affect dependency installation. Any real configuration remains rejected, preserving the target-controlled network boundary.

## Impact

OpenClaw automerge jobs can prepare the target toolchain without rejecting the repository's inert `.npmrc`. No service restart is required after merge; affected PRs can be retriggered with `@clawsweeper automerge`.

## Verification

- `pnpm run check`
- focused target-validation regression tests
- `autoreview --mode local` (clean after fixing its bare-CR security finding)
- changed-file `gitleaks` scans (no leaks)
